closed_trades.thesis: HPE is the most valuation-protected way to own the AI-server/networking buildout in a tape where reaccelerating inflation (CPI 4.27%) and a rising 10-year (4.56%) are punishing rich multiples. It trades at just ~12.2x forward earnings and 1.67x sales - the cheapest in the server group - after a record fiscal Q2 and the completed Juniper acquisition, which adds a scaled networking franchise. Sell-side has responded with a +40.5% 30-day upward EPS revision, yet the stock is consolidating (1m +1.4%) and sits 23.8% below its 52-week high, so estimates are rising while price has not re-rated. The same SMCI collapse (-29%) that helps Dell consolidates enterprise AI-server demand toward HPE as customers de-risk suppliers. With the last print already behind it (38 days ago) and no earnings inside the 40-day window, this is a clean cheap-re-rating swing.

Dell is the best risk/reward in an extended AI-server complex: it pairs elite momentum (+143% 3m, +202% 6m) with the cheapest valuation in the group (forward P/E ~20.9, P/S 2.2) and a constructive entry, having pulled back only 2.2% from its 20-day high while sitting 4.1% off its 52-week high near a buy point. What went right: the book avoided forcing a mediocre trade for a seventh straight day, and this afternoon's risk desk correctly vetoed a UNP BUY that looked clean on the surface -- a real Q2 beat plus a real same-day Canadian National rail-access agreement supporting the pending Norfolk Southern deal. What went wrong was reasoning, not data: the vetoed proposal's own thesis stated the CN agreement was 'signed one day earlier' when every dated headline in the bundle for that story was same-session (age_days 0.2-0.6, all 2026-07-24), and it cited a favorable RBC note from the same news pull while omitting a same-pull BNSF headline publicly attacking the exact merger-approval mechanism the trade was built on -- an unforced, checkable error that the risk desk had to catch instead of the reasoning process catching it first. The one change for next week: before finalizing any BUY thesis, I will explicitly cross-check every dated or sequenced claim in the catalysts and thesis fields against the actual age_days/published timestamps of the supporting headlines in the bundle, and label the timing as unverified rather than asserting a sequence the data doesn't support -- next Friday's review grades whether that habit actually prevented a repeat of this exact failure mode.

A same-day intraday quote (even just SPY/VIX last + % change, refreshed per run rather than once at prior close) would let the regime read catch a live risk-off day without relying on the agent remembering to search for it.

** `market_news` reported fetching 119 items (yahoo 49, cnbc 30, marketwatch 10, alpaca 30) and surfaced **15**, and because the cap keeps the *most recent* headlines, all 15 were published in the final 30 minutes before the gather — four of them the identical "12 [Sector] Stocks Moving In Tuesday's After-Market Session" template. The result is that the entire macro narrative of the session was dropped: not one headline about the US–Iran strikes that have crude up 6.55% in five sessions, and consequently `market_events.flags.counts.geopolitical` scored **0** on a night with a ten-day ceasefire proposal live. A required regime input returned a confident false negative, and I only caught it because I ran outside web research. Two cheap fixes: (1) **stratify the headline cap** — reserve half the slots for market-wide/macro stories and half for single-name, instead of sorting purely by recency; (2) **collapse templated Benzinga movers lists** ("N [Sector] Stocks Moving In...") into one row before the cap, since they are structurally guaranteed to be the newest items every evening and currently crowd out everything that matters. Secondary, and cheaper still: nothing in the bundle told me *where* today's money went — `momentum_health` correctly flagged "unwind" but a one-line leadership-rotation read (top and bottom sectors by same-day move) would have handed me the single most important fact of this session instead of my having to reconstruct it from 186 individual `pct_change_1d` fields.
